_about: Chunk-metadata sidecar for the context index. Maps a chunk id (manifest 'id', equal to the chunk topic) to hand-authored retrieval metadata that the ContextIndexGenerator merges over the auto-derived metadata. Metadata ABOUT the memory and docs, never a copy of their content; carries no tier and never edits AI-Memory.

memory.shared.index.summary: Map of the durable memory layout: shared rules, per-repo rules, and per-host notes, and which file owns which rule.
memory.shared.index.read_when: You are locating which memory file owns a rule, or deciding where a new memory belongs.

memory.shared.unified-project-memory.summary: The cross-tool memory core: what belongs in memory and the pointers to reporting, boundaries, diagnosis, and proof rules.
memory.shared.unified-project-memory.read_when: You are starting any session and orienting to the shared cross-tool rules.

memory.shared.unified-project-memory.wha.summary: What may become durable memory: only repeated behavior and hard lessons, never current work state, counts, or reverse-engineering findings.
memory.shared.unified-project-memory.wha.read_when: You are about to write or propose a new durable memory entry.

memory.shared.unified-project-memory.arm.summary: Pointer to the Armada session workflow and operational-asset rules; they are not duplicated in shared memory.
memory.shared.unified-project-memory.arm.read_when: You are operating Armada and need the session or asset procedure.

memory.shared.unified-project-memory.dia.summary: Diagnose from full context: read complete logs, compare against a known-good path, and separate environment from code before acting.
memory.shared.unified-project-memory.dia.read_when: You are diagnosing a failure or a suspected component defect.

memory.shared.unified-project-memory.run.summary: Runtime routing defaults: the Codex server model, the per-captain model record, and that Gemini is unavailable until authenticated.
memory.shared.unified-project-memory.run.read_when: You are choosing or changing a runtime or model for a session or captain.

memory.shared.unified-project-memory.sou.summary: Source comments state the rule not the incident: no dates, mission or voyage ids, commit hashes, or plan-block labels in committed code.
memory.shared.unified-project-memory.sou.read_when: You are writing or reviewing a source comment, test name, or log string.

memory.shared.audit-methods.summary: Two reusable audits: the coverage census before trusting a converged-to-zero result, and the test-suite growth and duplication census.
memory.shared.audit-methods.read_when: You are running or dispatching a coverage audit or a test-suite growth or duplication census.

memory.shared.sole-memory-source.scope-d.summary: Scope decides the folder for a new memory: shared, one repo, or one host; a lesson spanning two repos lives with the one that causes it.
memory.shared.sole-memory-source.scope-d.read_when: You are adding a memory and deciding which folder it belongs in.

memory.shared.sole-memory-source.where-t.summary: The per-host paths of the AI-Memory folder on the macOS workstation, the Windows workstation, and the Armada server.
memory.shared.sole-memory-source.where-t.read_when: You need the AI-Memory folder path on a specific host.

memory.shared.sole-memory-source.armada-.summary: How captains receive memory: a generated brief section points them at shared and their vessel repo folder, not the host notes.
memory.shared.sole-memory-source.armada-.read_when: You are configuring or reviewing how a captain receives memory rules.

memory.machine-notes.macos.summary: macOS workstation traps: the 1Password SSH agent will not sign from a sandbox, exFAT mode and AppleDouble noise, and the zsh and rebase pitfalls.
memory.machine-notes.macos.read_when: You are running git, pushing, or shell commands on the macOS workstation.

memory.repos.armada.readme.armada-memory.summary: Where current Armada platform behavior is owned (the repository docs), and that live counts and captain state do not live in memory.
memory.repos.armada.readme.armada-memory.read_when: You are looking for authoritative Armada platform behavior or the operator procedure entry points.

memory.repos.armada.readme.deploying-arm.summary: The full Armada deploy procedure: pause the scheduler, retain rollback image tags, rehearse against a restored database copy, and verify the running image.
memory.repos.armada.readme.deploying-arm.read_when: You are deploying, rebuilding, or redeploying the Armada admiral on the server.

memory.repos.armada.readme.autonomous-le.summary: The autonomous lead and Grok bot are retired; do not restore the lead timer, wake, or gateway during deployment.
memory.repos.armada.readme.autonomous-le.read_when: You are deploying Armada or reviewing lead, wake, or gateway configuration.

memory.repos.armada.readme.host-and-cont.summary: Host and container facts: the container mounts, nested per-dock siblings, the ubuntu runtime user, tmpfs, and the resident build servers.
memory.repos.armada.readme.host-and-cont.read_when: You are diagnosing a dock, sibling, mount, disk, or container-user problem on the server.

memory.repos.armada.readme.runtimes-and-.summary: Runtime and provider traps: the Mux runtime identity, provider throttling and billing holds that read as captain faults, and per-runtime key routing.
memory.repos.armada.readme.runtimes-and-.read_when: You are triaging a burst of fast captain failures or configuring an external provider.

memory.repos.armada.readme.briefs-and-ca.summary: Brief and captain-instruction rules: the prompt is a measured budget, deliver MCP explicitly per runtime, and never inline what the runtime auto-loads.
memory.repos.armada.readme.briefs-and-ca.read_when: You are writing a captain brief or configuring captain MCP delivery.

memory.repos.armada.readme.dispatch-and-.summary: Dispatch and assignment rules: captains are persona-locked, ReadyForDispatch is not permission, VesselIds must name exactly the receiving vessel.
memory.repos.armada.readme.dispatch-and-.read_when: You are dispatching an objective or diagnosing why a mission will not assign.

memory.repos.armada.readme.failures-that.summary: Failure classes that mimic others: Judge-stage failures, health-check synthesized exits, Infra misclassification, and merge-queue reverts.
memory.repos.armada.readme.failures-that.read_when: You are triaging a failed voyage, mission, or Check whose cause is unclear.

memory.repos.armada.readme.a-doc-comment.summary: A doc comment is not evidence a code path exists: verify the path by grepping the symbol and reading the caller, not the paragraph.
memory.repos.armada.readme.a-doc-comment.read_when: You are relying on a comment that names a trigger, cleanup, or code path.

memory.repos.armada.readme.architect-sta.summary: Architect-stage traps: the chain walk stops at dispatched boundaries, planner stages can overreach into code, and block ordering must be honored.
memory.repos.armada.readme.architect-sta.read_when: You are dispatching or diagnosing an Architect or multi-mission planner pipeline.

memory.repos.armada.readme.build-and-tes.summary: Armada build and test facts: land the CHANGELOG and docs in the same commit, run tests through dotnet run, and a test runs only when RunTest is called.
memory.repos.armada.readme.build-and-tes.read_when: You are building, testing, or landing a change in the Armada repository.

memory.repos.armada.readme.deciding-whet.summary: How to decide whether a stranded branch's work landed: cheap tests over-report work as missing; the reliable test is symbol-level.
memory.repos.armada.readme.deciding-whet.read_when: You are deciding whether a stranded or unlanded branch is safe to delete.

memory.repos.armada.readme.historical-sh.summary: Current docks provision per-mission siblings; the older shared-lease sibling model applies only when diagnosing an older deployment.
memory.repos.armada.readme.historical-sh.read_when: You are reasoning about dock siblings or a sibling-staleness failure.

memory.repos.armada.readme.model-tiering.summary: The model-tiering policy: two tiers, the ranked frontier Judge order, unranked specialists, and dispatch by logical tier not a concrete model.
memory.repos.armada.readme.model-tiering.read_when: You are choosing a model tier for dispatch or changing the tier configuration.

memory.repos.armada.readme.model-swap-pr.summary: The four surfaces to update when swapping a captain model, in order, so renamed captains stay dispatchable.
memory.repos.armada.readme.model-swap-pr.read_when: You are swapping or renaming a captain model.

memory.repos.armada.readme.captain-roste.summary: The captain roster by runtime and model; read live captain state from the platform, not from this table.
memory.repos.armada.readme.captain-roste.read_when: You need the captain roster or the runtime-to-model mapping.

memory.repos.armada.operational-assets.summary: Operator rules for playbooks, runbooks, workflow profiles, environments, personas, and pipelines, and the captain MCP boundary.
memory.repos.armada.operational-assets.read_when: You are creating or changing an Armada operational asset, or auditing an Architect pipeline.

memory.repos.armada.reviewer.closeout.summary: Closing incidents in both halves, reading RecoveryNotes before a duplicate rescue, and reconciling a stale Completed backlog row.
memory.repos.armada.reviewer.closeout.read_when: You are closing an incident or reconciling a stale backlog-state row.

memory.repos.jprodeobfuscator.readme.summary: JproDeobfuscator: the .xml.enc files are the source originals and the git-tracked decrypted plaintext lives beside them; cite the plaintext path and line count, never the .enc or a raw byte size.
memory.repos.jprodeobfuscator.readme.read_when: You are citing a JPRO catalogue, counting encrypted files, or writing a JproDeobfuscator brief.

docs.armada-ops.summary: The Armada operations reference: the Check-state table, dispatch mechanics, recovery, and papercut triage.
docs.armada-ops.read_when: You need authoritative Armada platform behavior, the Check-state table, or the papercut triage table.

docs.delivery-operations.summary: The delivery-operations reference: deployment, environments, and release procedure.
docs.delivery-operations.read_when: You are deploying or managing an Armada release or environment.

docs.context-index.summary: The context-index and progressive-disclosure reference: the core bundle, the manifest, and how retrieval widens beyond core.
docs.context-index.read_when: You are working on the context-index, the core bundle, or context retrieval.

docs.claude-code-as-orchestrator.summary: How to run Claude Code as an Armada orchestrator.
docs.claude-code-as-orchestrator.read_when: You are setting up or running Claude Code as the Armada orchestrator.

docs.codex-as-orchestrator.summary: How to run Codex as an Armada orchestrator.
docs.codex-as-orchestrator.read_when: You are setting up or running Codex as the Armada orchestrator.

memory.repos.armada.session-workflow.cur.summary: The current owner policy for an Armada session: direct-edit Armada, code indexing off, LocalMerge on managed vessels, and read captain state live.
memory.repos.armada.session-workflow.cur.read_when: You are starting an Armada operator session and need the current owner policy.

memory.repos.armada.session-workflow.cap.summary: Capture and dispatch work: verify the brief premise against the target tip, the thirteen-question preflight, stage-neutral descriptions, and idempotent stage handoff.
memory.repos.armada.session-workflow.cap.read_when: You are writing or dispatching a brief, verifying its premise, or preventing a stage-handoff or stale-premise contradiction.

memory.repos.armada.session-workflow.mon.summary: Monitor a voyage to a terminal state: subscribe rather than poll, watch running captain logs, and correct a wrong premise at the stage boundary before it reaches the next brief.
memory.repos.armada.session-workflow.mon.read_when: You are monitoring a dispatched voyage or mission, or a captain working on a wrong premise or base.

memory.repos.armada.session-workflow.che.summary: Check facts for an operator: dispatch arms Build and UnitTest, resolve every failed Check at the reviewed commit, and a retried flake resolves as Canceled.
memory.repos.armada.session-workflow.che.read_when: You are arming, reading, or resolving a Check on a voyage.

memory.repos.armada.session-workflow.tri.summary: Triage a failed mission or Check by class first: stage_base_missing, ineffective_rescue, test-host crash, a single deterministic failure, or a captain runtime error.
memory.repos.armada.session-workflow.tri.read_when: You are triaging a failed mission or a failed Check and need to classify the cause before recovery.

memory.repos.armada.session-workflow.rec.summary: Recover a failed mission: cancel a duplicate rescue, find the work by commit, prove the gate in a fresh worktree, land, and close the incident with evidence.
memory.repos.armada.session-workflow.rec.read_when: You are recovering a failed mission or landing recoverable work by operator.

memory.repos.armada.session-workflow.rev.summary: Review, land, and close: contain a failed voyage's branch in the same action, own every incident you dispatch, and a landing's last step is closing its row.
memory.repos.armada.session-workflow.rev.read_when: You are reviewing, landing, or closing Armada work, or containing a stranded branch.

memory.repos.eculink.readme.source-fidel.summary: EcuLink source fidelity: reproduce a source defect, do not correct it; printable-byte filters and length truncations are load-bearing; go through the landed parameter seam.
memory.repos.eculink.readme.source-fidel.read_when: You are porting or reviewing an EcuLink decoder, seed-key, or command for source fidelity.

memory.repos.eculink.readme.when-a-sourc.summary: When a source defect is a hang, crash, or unbounded resource use, do not silently reproduce or guard it: measure reachability from the catalogue and escalate to the owner.
memory.repos.eculink.readme.when-a-sourc.read_when: You found a source defect that hangs, crashes, or uses unbounded resources while porting EcuLink.

memory.repos.eculink.readme.port-defects.summary: EcuLink port defects cluster in response-handling logic (validation predicate, success or failure polarity, gate literal), not in request-frame bytes.
memory.repos.eculink.readme.port-defects.read_when: You are pre-verifying or reviewing an EcuLink command port beyond the request frame bytes.

memory.repos.eculink.readme.a-committed-.summary: An EcuLink committed source citation is the bare filename plus line range, never a decompiled-src path, assembly, or hash; one canonical shape, enforced by a test.
memory.repos.eculink.readme.a-committed-.read_when: You are writing or reviewing a committed EcuLink source citation comment.

memory.repos.source-glossary.readme.the-.summary: The SourceGlossary ledger gate's coverage depends on which roots resolve; a green gate proves the tree-dependent families only when the run states its resolved roots.
memory.repos.source-glossary.readme.the-.read_when: You are running or reviewing a SourceGlossary ledger pass, or a sibling-tree or root-resolution failure.

memory.repos.source-glossary.readme.a-fa.summary: A SourceGlossary guard that falls back to a twin file measures the wrong thing confidently; an unresolvable row is a named, counted skip, never a substitution.
memory.repos.source-glossary.readme.a-fa.read_when: You are diagnosing a SourceGlossary guard that disagrees between a green suite and a red executor on the same commit.

memory.repos.source-glossary.readme.a-ro.summary: A SourceGlossary row's evidence field is a repository-relative path to a file committed in SourceGlossary, never a source-tree citation.
memory.repos.source-glossary.readme.a-ro.read_when: You are writing or reviewing a SourceGlossary ledger row's evidence field.

memory.repos.source-glossary.readme.a-la.summary: A SourceGlossary landing-scope pin compares two fixed tips, never the current ledger; a guard that reads live global state is a debt every later pass pays.
memory.repos.source-glossary.readme.a-la.read_when: You are writing or reviewing a SourceGlossary landing-scope guard or a live-state pin.

memory.repos.otrbuddy.readme.otrbuddy-de.summary: OtrBuddy delivers every catalogue and EcuLink embeds none; add the bundle category first, then the EcuLink seam change in the same wave, or the build breaks.
memory.repos.otrbuddy.readme.otrbuddy-de.read_when: You are adding a catalogue category or reasoning about the OtrBuddy-to-EcuLink bundle path.

memory.repos.otrbuddy.readme.the-check-p.summary: The OtrBuddy check profile must provision every sibling a test probes; a sibling the profile does not provision is a gate that cannot go green.
memory.repos.otrbuddy.readme.the-check-p.read_when: You are diagnosing an OtrBuddy check that fails only in the executor, or a missing-sibling gate.

memory.repos.otrbuddy.readme.consumer-of.summary: OtrBuddy builds against EcuLink as a sibling; a CS0120/CS0117 gate failure after an EcuLink landing is a consumer break, and the consumer is sometimes the side that was wrong.
memory.repos.otrbuddy.readme.consumer-of.read_when: You are triaging an OtrBuddy build break after an EcuLink change.
